sin.name: csharp-null-forgiven
sin.description: The null-forgiving `!` on a value declared nullable — the compiler told the caller it may be null, and `!` silences it instead of deciding
sin.rule: Never silence a nullable warning with `!` — decide the missing case where the value is created, or handle it here.
sin.suggestion: Make the value non-nullable at its source, throw a named exception where it must exist, handle the null branch, or narrow it honestly (`OfType<T>()`, a pattern, `TryGetValue`).
